VAR-001.name: T### Series ID Convention
VAR-001.rationale: DEC-001: T prefix encodes chapter number, making IDs self-documenting for book replication
VAR-001.impact: All scripts, registry, docs, validation use T### throughout

VAR-002.name: R Shiny Instead of Plotly Dash
VAR-002.variant: R Shiny + Plotly (legacy from Shaikh Tonak project)
VAR-002.rationale: Pre-existing app with significant functionality; full rewrite not justified
VAR-002.impact: ShinyApp/ uses R ecosystem instead of Python Dash

VAR-003.name: Research Context in DPRs Instead of Separate JSON
VAR-003.variant: Research quotes and context embedded directly in DPR documents
VAR-003.rationale: DPRs already contain source quotes, HDARP linkages, and methodology context; separate JSON files would duplicate content
VAR-003.impact: Extenbook Research sheet populated from DPR content rather than research.json

VAR-004.name: N### Study Series ID Convention
VAR-004.variant: N### (N=external study, first two digits=study number, last digit=series within study)
VAR-004.rationale: Distinguishes book replication series (T###) from external study replication series (N###)
VAR-004.impact: 22 N-series across 8 external studies use N### IDs

VAR-005.name: 8-Phase NickyData Pipeline Instead of Anu Pipeline 10-Stage
VAR-005.rationale: NickyData collapses Anu Pipeline stages into a more compact orchestrator that better fits single-book replication projects
VAR-005.impact: run.py manages all phases; no separate Anu Pipeline state file

VAR-006.name: Matrix-Valued Series Skip Chopped/Extenbook
VAR-006.standard: All series produce Chopped CSV and Extenbook (Anu Output Standards)
VAR-006.variant: T401/T402 (IO matrices) are 85x85 benchmark matrices, not annual time series
VAR-006.rationale: The Chopped CSV format (Row 1 metadata, Row 2 IDs, Row 3+ annual data) does not apply to matrix-valued benchmark data
VAR-006.impact: T401 and T402 have CSV output but no chopped or extenbook artifacts

VAR-007.title: N-Series Decompositions Consolidated
VAR-007.description: All 26 N-series share a single consolidated STUDY_DECOMPOSITIONS.md file instead of individual N####_DECOMPOSITION.md files. This is because N-series are organized by study (8 studies, each with 2-5 series sharing the same processing batch in P19/P20), making individual decomposition files largely redundant.
